title: Troublesome company joins forces
odia:
ଓଲୁଅ ତିଆରେ ବଣ ସାରୁକୁ
ତୋର ମୋର ଯିବା ବିଭାଘରକୁ।
literal_meaning: Olua, the arum, urges the wild taro: “You and I will go to the wedding.”
meaning_odia: ଓଲୁଅ ଓ ବଣସାରୁ ଏକାଠି ବିଭାଘରକୁ ଯିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଦୁଇ ଅନିଷ୍ଟକାରୀ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ମେଳକୁ ବୁଝାଏ। ଦେଖାଯାଇଥିବା ସଂକଳନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଅନୁସାରେ, ସେମାନେ ଏକାଠି ହେଲେ ଭଲ କାମରେ ବିଘ୍ନ ଘଟିପାରେ।
explanation: Two plants are given voices and set off together for a wedding. The inspected Odia Vasa gloss applies the pairing to two troublesome people whose combined presence disrupts a good undertaking. The emphasis is on their joining forces, not merely resembling one another.
usage_example: Two people who repeatedly derail meetings decide to attend the same planning session together. Someone might use the saying to express concern about their combined disruption. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: The wedding supplies the scene of a shared occasion, while the plants become a pair of would-be guests. The compact exchange makes an alliance visible before the source gloss turns it into a warning about company that causes trouble.

graphic.caption: An imagined pair of plant guests approaches a wedding setting together.

odia_summary: ଦୁଇ ଅନିଷ୍ଟକାରୀ ଲୋକ ଏକାଠି ହୋଇ ଭଲ କାମରେ ବିଘ୍ନ କରିବା।
english_summary: Two troublesome people together can disrupt a good undertaking.
